headline: High: slim’s shell/network/write privileges can amplify any shared-workspace interaction with the non-runnable prompt-writing repo into data leakage and cascading misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between agent_a and agent_b. agent_a is a non-runnable content-writing repo with empty io_surfaces, while agent_b uses stdin/stdout and filesystem but no clipboard or MCP bridge is shown. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is introduced between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_a outputs are manually pasted into agent_b prompts, prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts.
Disable any shared clipboard or queue integration.
Review any future bridge for provenance tagging.
requires-engineering: add content provenance filters before agent_b consumes external text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and is non-runnable, while agent_b reads/writes filesystem artifacts and handles registry credentials and private keys. There is no documented shared workspace or direct data flow from agent_a to agent_b, so leakage is not default; if a shared workspace is added, agent_b could expose files it processes.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, agent_b can read files that agent_a may reference.
IF sensitive files are present in agent_b's workspace, its broad network egress can transmit them.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace.
Run agent_b on a scrubbed copy of inputs.
Restrict network egress during sensitive runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or runtime capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. agent_b can write the filesystem and execute shells, but modify_git_state is false and no shared mutable target is documented. The only plausible conflict is if an operator points both at the same writable directory, which is unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF agent_b is run against a git checkout with external writers, coordination issues can appear.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same path.
Do not run agent_b inside a shared git worktree.
Check for existing files before writes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a prompt-engineering content repo, so its outputs are likely advisory text rather than authoritative facts. agent_b is an interactive CLI that executes commands, but no evidence shows it automatically trusts agent_a. A cascade would require operator or orchestration to feed agent_a text into agent_b without verification, which is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF agent_a text is copied into agent_b as commands or instructions, agent_b may act on it.
IF an orchestrator treats agent_a output as authoritative, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before executing agent_a-derived instructions.
Separate drafting from execution roles.
Use a checklist to verify commands before running them.
Log provenance for any text passed between agents.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before agent_b executes derived actions.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b explicitly handles certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials, while agent_a has no documented data classes or compliance controls. Because agent_b also has broad network egress, any sensitive material in its workspace can leave the environment; the absence of documented residency or retention controls on either side makes the compliance gap material, though not proven critical.
conditions: IF agent_b processes PHI, regulated secrets, or EU PII, residency and retention controls must be verified.
IF agent_b uploads workspace contents to external APIs, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in agent_b's workspace.
Rotate any secrets exposed during testing.
Restrict network egress for compliance-sensitive runs.
Document retention and deletion handling.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention.
